inlines.v: LOQUA'CIOUS, adjective [Latin loquax, from loquor, to speak. Eng. to clack.] 1. Talkative; given to continual talking. Loquacious, brawling ever in the wrong. 2. Speaking; noisy. Bling British bards, with volant touch, traverse loquacious strings. 3. Apt to blab and disclose secrets.
